tools.name: send_push
tools.description: Send a push notification to one user (user_id), a list (user_ids, up to 1,000), a topic, or everyone (all: true). Give exactly one target. A push to one user, sent now, answers with its result at once; others answer with status sending or scheduled. With a test key (sk_test_) only test devices recei

tools.name: get_push
tools.description: One push by id: status, devices, sent and failed, per platform.

tools.name: list_pushes
tools.description: Pushes, newest first. On the Free plan only pushes still to go are listed (no delivery logs).

tools.name: cancel_push
tools.description: Cancel a push that is scheduled and has not started sending.

tools.name: register_device
tools.description: Store a device's push token under your user id. Android and iOS tokens come from the Firebase or Apple SDK; for web, token is the PushSubscription as JSON.

tools.name: list_devices
tools.description: The devices registered for one user id, newest first, with platform and whether each is trusted for approvals.

tools.name: remove_device
tools.description: Remove one device by id; it gets no more pushes.

tools.name: list_topics
tools.description: Topics with how many users each has.

tools.name: subscribe_topic
tools.description: Add a user to a topic. The topic exists once it has a user.

tools.name: unsubscribe_topic
tools.description: Take a user off a topic.

tools.name: list_templates
tools.description: Saved push templates with their fields.

tools.name: get_template
tools.description: One template by name.

tools.name: save_template
tools.description: Create or replace a template. Put {{field}} where a value goes, or {{field|default}} for one with a fallback.

tools.name: delete_template
tools.description: Delete a template by name. Pushes already made from it are not changed.

tools.name: create_approval
tools.description: Send an approval request to the user's trusted phone, with number matching. The user must have a phone enrolled through the SignOps SDK.

tools.name: get_approval
tools.description: An approval request's status: pending, approved, denied, expired or cancelled.

tools.name: cancel_approval
tools.description: Cancel a pending approval request.

tools.name: list_passkeys
tools.description: The passkeys registered for one user id.

tools.name: get_authenticator
tools.description: Whether a user has an authenticator app (TOTP) confirmed, when it was last used, backup codes left, and whether wrong codes have locked them.

tools.name: remove_authenticator
tools.description: Remove a user's authenticator app and backup codes, for a lost phone. They can enrol again.

tools.name: unlock_user
tools.description: Clear the lock that five wrong codes in 15 minutes put on a user, and their count of wrong codes.

tools.name: export_user
tools.description: Everything SignOps holds on one user id as JSON: devices (tokens shortened), topics, passkeys, authenticator status, approvals of the last 90 days, consent history and pushes sent to them.

tools.name: get_consent
tools.description: The latest consent answer per purpose for one user, like marketing_push, and the history.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: send_push · Private data: register_device, export_user · Public sink: send_push, create_approval · Destructive: remove_device, delete_template, remove_authenticator.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: send_push · Private data: register_device, export_user · Public sink: send_push, create_approval · Destructive: remove_device, delete_template, remove_authenticator

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
